explanations: terra: Those who follow guidance sent from God need not fear or grieve, giving the prayer for guidance the character of a path to safety.

luna: The section’s “dāllīn” are those who fail to find the way and its middle; this verse says “ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ” of someone who has lost the middle of the way. It makes the image of losing the road’s center explicit in Quranic wording. | terra: `ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ` directly names losing the middle of the road, the inverse of remaining in the road's centre.

luna: Amid objections to the change of prayer direction, the verse says “يَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” The disputed direction makes the straight path a divinely set orientation, rather than a route established by every onlooker’s judgment. | terra: In the change of prayer direction, God guides whom He wills to a straight path, placing guidance within a scene of communal orientation.
terra: The community is made `أُمَّةً وَسَطًا`; its middle position gives a social counterpart to the section's insistence on staying in the middle of the road.
terra: The command not to follow `خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ` makes Satan's preceding footsteps a rival trail across the earth's provided ground.
terra: People insist on what they found their fathers upon even when those fathers neither understood nor were guided, warning that a well-worn inherited practice need not be a true route.
terra: The community is told to enter wholly and not follow Satan's `خُطُوَات`; communal wholeness is set against taking the adversary's footsteps.

luna: After describing people as one community who then differed, the verse says God guided believers to the truth in their disputes and “يَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” This sets the section’s shared road against divisions that leave people without a common way.

luna: After affirming belief in the clear verses, the speakers ask, “لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا.” This prayer not to deviate after guidance extends the section’s request “ihdinā” through to its fear of losing the way.

luna: Jesus says “فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ.” The verse explicitly places worship on the straight path, making audible the section’s adjacent roots for “we worship” and “straight.” | terra: Jesus says `فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ`, the same worship-as-road claim made in 36:61.
terra: People who turn believers from God's way and seek it `عِوَجًا` oppose the straight line of the requested path by trying to bend it.

luna: The verse says whoever holds fast to God “فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” That image of holding fast alongside being guided makes the route something one remains attached to, echoing the section’s continued walking without leaving the way. | terra: Holding fast to God results in being guided `إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ`, naming how a traveller is kept on the road.
terra: Holding together to God's rope and not becoming divided gives the one shared course a communal form opposed to scattering.
terra: God promises to guide believers to the `سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ`; the path is a way already travelled by earlier communities.
terra: Some call unbelievers `أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا`; the claim provides a false assessment of which way is more rightly guided.

luna: In a passage about obeying God and the Messenger, the verse promises “وَلَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا.” This directly joins obedience to being guided onto a straight route. | terra: Obedience to God and the Messenger is answered with guidance to `صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا`, so the guide and the walked course are joined.

luna: The next verse names the prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous as good company for those who obey God and the Messenger. It completes 4:68 by showing a community of exemplars walking the straight route the section calls the path of those granted favor. | terra: Those who obey join the people upon whom God has bestowed favour, `أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم`; it identifies the blessed company named as the road's people in 1:7.

luna: The verse warns against opposing the Messenger after guidance has become clear and “يَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ.” This names the believers’ shared way as a route one can either follow or leave, directly sharpening the section’s “path of those You favored.” | terra: Turning aside from the Messenger and following a course other than `سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ` makes the believers' way a communal route with a grave contrary direction.

luna: The verse says God will admit believers to mercy and grace and “يَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا.” It makes the section’s destination-bearing sense of hidaya explicit: the route leads “to Him.” | terra: Those who believe and hold fast are guided toward God on `صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا`; the path is explicitly oriented toward its destination.
terra: Breaking the covenant is described as `ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ`, another exact loss of the middle/even way.

luna: In the context of the Book clarifying God’s pleasure, the verse says God guides followers to “سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ,” brings them from darkness to light, and guides them “إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” It connects following, multiple routes of peace, and arrival at a straight way. | terra: By the Book God guides seekers of His approval to `سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ`; guidance supplies several routes whose end is peace.
terra: Different communities are given `شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا`; this makes a boundary on reading every plurality of religious ways as the scattered roads rejected in 6:153.
terra: The condemned are `أَضَلُّ عَن سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ`, using the even road as the measure from which a way can be lost.

luna: The verse warns the People of the Book not to follow a people who “ضَلُّوا عَن سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ.” Its context links deviation to following others’ desires, sharpening the section’s contrast between the favored community’s route and those who have left it. | terra: People who went astray and led many astray have strayed from `سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ`, a collective version of departure from the road's middle.
terra: The appeal to what fathers were found doing persists even when they lacked knowledge and guidance, another boundary on treating habitual tracks as reliable.
terra: The believer is told that those who have strayed cannot harm them if they are guided, keeping the guided traveller distinct from surrounding wanderers.

luna: In a passage comparing people who are deaf and dumb in darkness with those God wills to guide, the verse says He may place a person “عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” It connects the section’s lost way and guided way to the contrast between disorientation and a clear route. | terra: God may leave one to stray or put one on a straight path; the exact alternative makes hidayah and dalal two opposed directions.

luna: The section describes one who cannot find the road or home; this verse depicts a person “حَيْرَانَ” on earth, while companions call him “إِلَى الْهُدَى ائْتِنَا.” The lost traveller and those calling him back make the contrast between disorientation and a guided community concrete. | terra: The person left `فِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ` is called `إِلَى الْهُدَى` by companions, a full scene of the lost traveller and a community on the way.

luna: After naming prophets and their forefathers, the verse says “وَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” The guided predecessors give the section’s “path of those You favored” named exemplars who have already been led along it. | terra: Chosen ancestors, descendants, and brothers are guided to a straight path, furnishing a line of prior walkers for the communal path.
terra: After the guided prophets are named, the Messenger is told to follow `هُدَاهُمْ`; guidance is received by following those who went before.

luna: The verse says God made the stars so people may “لِتَهْتَدُوا بِهَا” in the darkness of land and sea. This gives the section’s route markers a concrete counterpart: heavenly signs help a traveller keep direction when the way is hard to see. | terra: Stars are made so people may be guided through the darknesses of land and sea, a navigation scene that supplements the landmarks and star of 16:16.

luna: After describing the person God guides as having an opened breast and the one left astray as constricted, the verse says “هَٰذَا صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًا.” It links the section’s straight route with the contrasting states of those able or unable to receive guidance. | terra: `هَٰذَا صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًا` identifies the Lord's road as straight after distinguishing the guided from the straying.
terra: `دَارُ السَّلَامِ` is theirs with their Lord, completing the preceding Lord's path with the home to which that protected guidance belongs.
terra: In the command concerning God's provision, people are again forbidden to follow Satan's `خُطُوَات`; a false leader's tracks oppose the straight path.

luna: The section contrasts a shared, straight road with people scattering in every direction; the command says “هَٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ” and warns that following “السُّبُلَ” divides people from His way. The many paths make the communal, already trodden route a practical choice of what to follow. | terra: `صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا` is one road to follow, while `السُّبُل` split walkers away from it; it makes the requested common, straight track the opposite of dispersal.

luna: The Prophet is told to say “هَدَانِي رَبِّي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ” and to name it “دِينًا قِيَمًا.” The verse brings guidance, a straight route, and an upright way of life together, as the section’s root echoes suggest. | terra: `هَدَانِي ... إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا` explicitly brings guidance, the straight path, and an upright lived religion into one claim.

luna: The section’s road is a route someone must keep following; Iblis swears “لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ,” placing an adversary directly on it. This shows that a clear road can still be obstructed. | terra: Iblis vows to sit on `صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ`; the danger is placed directly upon the road whose guidance is sought.

luna: After 7:16 places Iblis on the straight path, this verse names the approaches “مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ” and “مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ” and from right and left. The linked verse completes the ambush scene by showing pressure from around the route. | terra: The attack comes from front, back, right, and left, completing the preceding road-ambush as pressure from every side of a straight course.
terra: One party is guided while another's error is due; the latter take devils as allies and think themselves guided, an account of misoriented walkers.
terra: The people of the Garden say God guided them `لِهَٰذَا`; arrival in the garden gives the guided path its reached destination.
terra: Wrongdoers bar people from God's way and seek it crooked, a direct contrary action to guiding someone along a straight road.

luna: The section’s scattered people go every way, while this command forbids sitting “بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ” to threaten people and turn them from Allah’s way. It gives the image a social counterpart: a route can be blocked and its travellers diverted. | terra: People are told not to sit at every road, threaten travellers, block God's way, and seek it crooked; it closely parallels Iblis stationed on the straight road.

luna: The verse says the arrogant turn from signs, do not take “سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ” when they see it, and take “سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ” instead. Its opposition between visible routes explains how a person can see markers and still choose the way that leads astray. | terra: Those who reject signs do not take the way of right conduct even when they see it, but take the way of error; sight of two roads still requires right orientation.
terra: Among Moses' people is a community that guides by truth and judges by it, a people that carries guidance together.
terra: A community guides by truth and acts justly by it, showing a people that carries guidance together rather than merely receiving it.
terra: Whomever God leaves astray has no guide, making the absence of a hādī the condition of wandering.
terra: The foremost emigrants and helpers are followed by later people in good conduct, giving the communal path the human order of those ahead and those who follow.
terra: Their Lord guides believers by their faith and they arrive amid the rivers of bliss; guidance here has the Garden as its reached dwelling.

luna: The section says guidance shows both the road and the home it reaches; here God calls to “دَارِ السَّلَامِ” and guides whom He wills “إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” The destination named beside the path fills out where the guided journey leads. | terra: God calls to `دَارِ السَّلَامِ` and guides whom He wills to a straight path, joining the destination-home to the guidance that reaches it.
terra: After truth there is only `الضَّلَالُ`, a stark directional boundary that clarifies why the prayer refuses the state of the lost.
terra: The ayah asks whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy of being followed, giving the section's guide-who-goes-ahead an explicit follower relation.
terra: Moses and Aaron are commanded `فَاسْتَقِيمَا` and not to follow the way of the unknowing, making steadfast progress and a contrary trail explicit.
terra: Those who bar from God's path and seek crookedness make the road's straightness an object of active opposition.

luna: Hud says of his Lord, “إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ,” while declaring his trust in Him. The phrase presents the straight way as belonging to the Lord who governs every creature, adding a claim about the route’s authority beyond the traveller’s direction. | terra: `إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ` makes the Lord's rule itself a straight course, grounding the traveller's road in divine constancy.
terra: Pharaoh `يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ` and brings them to the Fire; the leader who goes before is a dark reversal of the hādī who leads a people home.
terra: `فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ` commands the Prophet and those who turned with him to remain straight, giving the route its continuing communal practice.
terra: Worship of God is called `الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ`; it ties the section's worship, religion, and uprightness together without separating them.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to say “أَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي.” It pairs a caller who sees clearly with people who follow him, echoing the section’s guide and the community walking behind him. | terra: `هَٰذِهِ سَبِيلِي` is a proclaimed way to God shared by the speaker and those who follow him, a guide and a company on one route.

luna: The verse says “وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ,” naming a guide for every people. It gives the section’s “hādī” a communal setting: guidance is associated with someone who leads a people, not only private direction. | terra: `وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ` makes a guide belong to every people, linking a guide in front with the communal character of the path.

luna: The Book is sent to bring people from darkness into light and “إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ.” It gives the section’s guided route a revealed guide and an explicit movement from obscurity toward God’s way. | terra: The Book brings people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission, `إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ`, a passage led toward God.
terra: Those who bar from God's way and seek it `عِوَجًا` actively turn the route crooked, directly opposing the unbent straight path.

luna: The messengers say God has “هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا” and that they will endure the harm done to them. It connects being shown a route with remaining on it through opposition, a pressure implied by the section’s insistence on continuing without deviation. | terra: The messengers say God has guided them to their `سُبُلَنَا`; divine guidance is described as a way on which they can rely and endure.
terra: `هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ` names a straight path directed to God, sharpening the section's claim that knowing a road includes knowing where it reaches.
terra: Satan is denied authority over God's devoted servants, completing the straight-path declaration in 15:41 with a boundary against the tempter's claim.

luna: The verse says “وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ” and that some ways are “جَائِرٌ.” Its distinction between the directed way and crooked routes gives the section’s straight path a clear boundary against deviation. | terra: `وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ` sets the right direction of the way against a way that is `جَائِرٌ`, making straightness and deviation properties of routes.

luna: The section pictures a traveller finding the route and its destination; here God places mountains, rivers, and “سُبُلًا” in the earth “لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ.” Paths are part of the created landscape by which travellers can find their way. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and `سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ` make a physical landscape in which routes exist so that people can find their way.

luna: The section’s “worlds” carries the dictionary echo of a landmark, and this verse names “عَلَامَاتٍ” and says people find their way by the stars. It joins markers and guidance in the very scene the image evokes. | terra: `عَلَامَاتٍ` and the star by which people `يَهْتَدُونَ` give the traveller's landmarks and navigation which the section hears beside `ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ`.
terra: Each community receives the command to worship God and shun false gods; some are guided and others deserve error, joining worship to the hidayah/dalal divide.

luna: The bee is told “فَاسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا.” Its paths of the Lord made easy or tractable echo the section’s image of a road made walkable and subdued, and extend the path image to a creature following a route. | terra: The bee is commanded to follow the ways of its Lord, `سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا`; paths are expressly made easy to be traversed.

luna: The parable contrasts a dependent person unable to accomplish anything with one who “يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” It makes the straight-path figure an active, upright agent, adding force to the section’s embodied image of walking rather than merely knowing. | terra: The one who commands justice and is on a straight path contrasts with a dependent person who brings no good, giving uprightness a guiding public speech.
terra: Abraham is grateful for divine favours, chosen, and guided to a straight path; a blessed forebear becomes a prior walker on that way.
terra: After Abraham is named as guided to a straight path, the Prophet is commanded to follow his religion; a later traveller is placed behind that prior guide.
terra: The Messenger is commanded to call to the way of his Lord, while God knows who has strayed from it and who is guided.

luna: The verse says the Quran “يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ.” The same root as “المستقيم” describes the guidance as leading toward what is most upright, making the revelation itself a guide for the section’s straight route. | terra: The Quran guides to what is `أَقْوَمُ`, extending the section's straightness root from the road to the Book's most upright direction.
terra: One blind in this life is more astray from the way in the next; lost direction is pictured as an inability to see the route.
terra: The Book is `قَيِّمًا` and free of `عِوَجًا`; by an explicit bridge, its upright, unbent speech parallels the section's straight-line account of `مُسْتَقِيم`.
terra: Whomever God guides is guided, and one left astray finds no guiding protector; a guide's absence is linked to being lost.
terra: Moses and his companion return `عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمَا` after losing their way to the meeting-place, an actual recovery of route by retracing footprints.

luna: Moses asks the knowledgeable servant, “هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا.” In their journey, a learner explicitly asks to follow a guide in order to learn right direction, paralleling the section’s guide who walks ahead. | terra: Moses asks to follow a servant so he may be taught `رُشْدًا`; the scene concretely pairs a follower with a teacher who can lead him rightly.

luna: Jesus says “إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ.” Like the section’s sequence from worship to the request for a path, this verse names worship itself as that path. | terra: `فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ` again makes shared worship the road itself.

luna: Abraham tells his father “فَاتَّبِعْنِي أَهْدِكَ صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا.” A guide walks ahead and invites another to follow, closely matching the section’s account of hidaya as showing a route and leading along it. | terra: Abraham asks his father to follow him so that he may guide him to `صِرَاطٍ سَوِيٍّ`, a guide addressing a particular traveller.
terra: `الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ` identifies the divinely favoured prophets whose company gives content to the people of 1:7.
terra: God made the earth a resting ground and placed `سُبُلًا` through it, giving the section's path a made, traversable ground.
terra: Moses is told to lead God's servants by night and make for them a dry path through the sea; a guide ahead of a people receives a traversable road at the obstruction.
terra: Pharaoh led his people astray and `مَا هَدَىٰ`, naming the failed leader of a community as the opposite of the guiding one.

luna: After the account of Adam, God says “فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ.” It directly links following revealed guidance with not losing the way, the outcome sought by the section’s prayer. | terra: Whoever follows divine guidance will neither go astray nor suffer; following and not becoming `ضَلَّ` define remaining on the course.
terra: The final question asks who are companions of `الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ` and who is guided, directly coupling the even road and hidayah.
terra: The earth has firm mountains and broad mountain-pass roads, `فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا`, so that people may be guided; paths are formed through terrain for travel.
terra: Abraham's household are made leaders who guide by God's command; their exemplary guidance joins a people with leaders who go before them.
terra: Whoever takes Satan as ally is led astray and then guided to the punishment of the Blaze, a counter-guidance with the wrong end.
terra: God guides whom He wills to a straight path through clear verses, connecting disclosed signs to route-finding.
terra: They are guided to good speech and to `صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيدِ`, so the same hidayah reaches a named path of God.
terra: Pilgrims come on foot and on lean mounts from every deep mountain pass to the House, giving road-walking a shared destination.

luna: After speaking of those given knowledge recognizing the revelation as truth, the verse says “وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهَادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” It presents belief as a community led onto the route the section asks to follow. | terra: God guides believers to a straight path after they recognize the revelation as truth, making the path a response to received guidance.
terra: The Prophet is told to call to his Lord while being upon straight guidance, making his address an invitation from a sure course.
terra: The Messenger's call is explicitly `إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ`, a voice inviting hearers onto the route.
terra: Those who reject the hereafter are `لَنَاكِبُونَ عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ`, turning away from the path just named in 23:73.
terra: Following Satan's `خُطُوَات` leads toward indecency and wrong; the ayah makes visible why not every trail left before a walker should be followed.

luna: After saying God has sent clear signs, the verse says “وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” The signs and guidance together echo the section’s route and its landmarks, while the verse makes clear that guidance is granted by God. | terra: God guides whom He wills to a straight path after sending clarifying signs, joining signs and route-finding.
terra: Obedience to the Messenger yields guidance, identifying following the one sent ahead as the way to be guided.

luna: On Judgment Day the wrongdoer regrets “يَا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا.” His wish to have taken a way with the Messenger makes the section’s path of a guided community painfully concrete: the route depended on whom he chose to follow.

luna: The regret in 25:27 is explained when the speaker says “لَقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ الذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ جَاءَنِي.” This neighbor identifies the companion who led him away from the route he wishes he had taken with the Messenger.

luna: The Messenger says he asks no reward except that whoever wills may “يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا.” This makes the way a chosen route toward the Lord, complementing the section’s claim that guidance shows both a path and where it leads. | terra: Whoever wills may take a way to his Lord; the road is explicitly an approach toward its divine destination.
terra: At the sea Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him, a traveller's assurance at a blocked route.

luna: When Moses’ people fear they will be overtaken, God commands him to strike the sea and promises “طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا.” The dry route through the sea is a concrete path opened for a group to follow under a guide.
terra: Satan has barred a people from the way, so they are not guided; their worship is a concrete rival route to worship on the straight path.
terra: The one who guides through land-and-sea darkness and sends winds is invoked; this is the traveller's disorientation answered by guidance through signs.

luna: As Moses heads toward Midian, he hopes “أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ.” The phrase “middle of the way” directly clarifies the section’s dictionary image of keeping to the road’s middle while travelling. | terra: Moses is travelling toward Madyan and asks to be guided to `سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ`, staging the section's road-finding at the middle of a way.
terra: One who follows desire without guidance from God is called most astray, opposing a shown road to self-directed drift.

luna: The verse promises “لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا” to those who strive for God and says God is with the doers of good. Its plural “ways” ties continued effort to being led, complementing the section’s road as a practice walked over time. | terra: Those who strive are guided to God's `سُبُلَنَا`; the plural ways are paths opened by sustained walking rather than an abstract fact alone.
terra: Turning one's face toward the upright religion, `الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ`, gives religion the directed and upright stance heard in the path image.
terra: Those who split their religion into factions turn habitual religion into scattered parties, the social contrary to one walked road.
terra: `فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ الْقَيِّمِ` gives the upright religion the directed posture of a traveller setting his face toward a course.

luna: In the warning against obeying parents who press toward associating partners with God, the verse still says “وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ.” It gives a concrete model to follow along a path, matching the section’s communal route while marking a contrary direction. | terra: `وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ` commands following the way of one who turns to God, then names the return to Him as the destination.
terra: One who submits to God and does good has grasped the firmest handhold, a concrete image of being kept secure on the directed course.

luna: The verse says God made leaders “يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا” when they were patient and certain of His signs. It supplies the section’s guide who goes ahead with a community, grounded in patience and recognized signs. | terra: From among them God made leaders guiding by His command when they were patient and certain, a communal line of guides ahead of others.
terra: The followers say their leaders and great ones led them astray `عَنِ السَّبِيلِ`, the inverse of following a hādī on the road.

luna: Those given knowledge recognize the revelation as truth from the Lord and “يَهْدِي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ.” The verse joins a revealed guide to the destination-bearing straight route the section describes. | terra: The revealed Book guides `إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ`, uniting scripture, guidance, and a destination-bearing path.
terra: The speaker sets guidance against manifest error between two parties, preserving the path's decisive fork even without a named road.
terra: The arrogant ask whether they prevented followers from guidance after it came; guidance can be obstructed by leaders who redirect a group.
terra: The Messenger is declared to be upon a straight path; his standing on it gives the requesting community a guide already on the road.
terra: `اتَّبِعُوا مَن لَّا يَسْأَلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ` gives a concrete rule for choosing whom to follow: the guides are themselves guided.

luna: The section distinguishes the path of those granted favor from those who stray; this address tells the criminals “وَامْتَازُوا الْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ.” In the same passage, 36:61 names worship as the straight path, so the separation marks the boundary around that call. | terra: The command for criminals to separate begins the nearby scene in which worship, straight path, and mass misguidance are distinguished.
terra: `أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ ... أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا الشَّيْطَانَ` supplies the opposite worship immediately before worship of God is named the straight path.

luna: The address to Adam’s children says “وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ.” The shared formulation directly joins worship to the straight route, as the section’s movement from “نَعْبُدُ” to “الصِّرَاطَ” does. | terra: `اعْبُدُونِي هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ` makes worship itself the straight path, joining the movement from `نَعْبُدُ` to `ٱلصِّرَاط`.

luna: Immediately after identifying worship as a straight path in 36:61, the verse says Satan “أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا.” It supplies the section’s contrary image of many people led away from the road. | terra: Satan has `أَضَلَّ ... جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا`; beside the command to worship, it shows a great human multitude diverted from that path.

luna: The section asks for guidance along the way of those granted favor; here the command is “فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ.” The same guiding and path language leads to the opposite destination, exposing guidance as inseparable from where a route ends. | terra: `فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ` reverses the requested guidance: the same leading and road vocabulary now reaches the Fire.
terra: David is told not to follow desire lest it lead him astray from God's way; just judgment is set on the side of staying clear of a diverted route.
terra: Those who avoid false gods and turn to God receive good news, a movement away from the false worship opposed to the path of worship.
terra: Those who listen and follow the best of speech are the ones God has guided, giving guidance the form of attentive following.
terra: An Arabic Quran without crookedness is described as a means of mindfulness; its absence of `عِوَج` gives a textual counterpart to an unbent course.
terra: The believing man fears that Pharaoh may cause corruption or make the people's religion prevail; within the later speech he offers a competing road of right conduct.

luna: The believing man in Pharaoh’s household says “اتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ.” His invitation to follow him along the way of right guidance gives the section’s leading guide a speaker and a concrete communal setting. | terra: The believing man says, `اتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ`: followers are invited behind a speaker who will lead them to the way of right conduct.
terra: The next appeal contrasts his call to salvation with their call to the Fire, supplying the opposed destinations to the guidance in 40:38.
terra: The Messenger says the deity is one and commands, `فَاسْتَقِيمُوا إِلَيْهِ`; steadfastness is expressly directed toward God as the route's end.
terra: Thamud were offered guidance but preferred blindness to it, a deliberate exchange of seeing the route for losing it.
terra: Those who say God is Lord and then remain steadfast (`اسْتَقَامُوا`) are met by angels, making continuance an enduring communal stance.
terra: Communities are told to establish religion and not divide in it; daily religion is kept from becoming the scattered groups opposed to one way.

luna: The Prophet is commanded “فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ” and not to follow others’ desires after knowledge has come. The same root as “المستقيم” makes straightness an ongoing stance of not leaving the course. | terra: The Prophet is told to call, remain steadfast as commanded, and not follow their desires, joining continued straightness to refusal of rival directions.

luna: The verse tells the Prophet “وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” It gives the section’s guide who walks ahead a Quranic instance: the Messenger leads people toward the straight route. | terra: The Prophet is told, `وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ`, explicitly casting him as one who guides others toward the straight route.

luna: The next verse calls it “صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ” and says to Him belongs what is in the heavens and earth and all affairs return. It completes 42:52 by naming whose route it is and the destination to which it returns. | terra: The next ayah names that route `صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ`, completing 42:52 by identifying the road's owner and end.

luna: The verse says God made the earth a resting place and made “سُبُلًا” in it “لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ.” This grounds the section’s road and guidance in the earth’s traversable landscape. | terra: God made paths in the earth `لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ`; the route and the act of finding it occur together.
terra: A people claim to be guided while following the `آثَار` of their ancestors, a critical counterpart to a path marked by earlier feet.
terra: The same ancestral `آثَار` are named as the tracks a community imitates, continuing the question of whether inherited traces truly guide.
terra: The messenger asks whether a more guided way than the fathers' way would still be refused, exposing inherited route-following as a possible error.
terra: Devils bar people from the way while the people think themselves guided, a concentrated image of confident misorientation.

luna: The Prophet is told “فَاسْتَمْسِكْ بِالَّذِي أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” Holding fast to revelation while already on the straight path matches the section’s account of continuing without turning aside. | terra: Holding fast to revelation is paired with being on a straight path, showing how one stays rather than leaves the course.
terra: `وَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ` warns against Satan's turning people aside immediately before Jesus states worship as the straight path in 43:64.

luna: Jesus says “فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ.” This second Quranic formulation, in a passage affirming God as Lord, makes the section’s root echo between worship and the straight road explicit. | terra: Jesus' command `فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ` joins service and the one straight course.

luna: God says, “ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْرِ فَاتَّبِعْهَا,” then forbids following the desires of those without knowledge. The revealed law is framed as a course to follow, a parallel to the section’s path as practiced movement rather than mere knowledge. | terra: The Prophet is placed upon a `شَرِيعَةٍ` and told to follow it rather than the desires of the unknowing, a prescribed course with a contrary divergence.
terra: One who makes desire a god is left astray despite knowledge; worshiping desire reverses the worship-path ordered in the section.
terra: Those who affirm God and then remain steadfast are promised no fear or grief, giving `اسْتَقَامُوا` the continuing shape of the straight course.

luna: The jinn describe the revelation as confirming Moses’ scripture and “يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ وَإِلَىٰ طَرِيقٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” Their report gives the straight way a revealed guide and shows others recognizing that route. | terra: The Quran guides to truth and `إِلَىٰ طَرِيقٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ`, another direct union of revealed guide and straight way.
terra: God increases those who are guided in guidance and gives them their mindfulness, depicting the path as a course whose clarity can grow.
terra: Those who turn back after guidance has become clear abandon a course once shown, a temporal reverse of continuing without deviation.

luna: The verse says God forgives the Prophet and “يَهْدِيَكَ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا.” It frames the Messenger himself as guided along a straight route, complementing the section’s sense of a guide who has a way to lead others on. | terra: God's completed favour upon the Messenger includes `وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا`, directly joining bestowed favour, guidance, and the straight path.
terra: Desires and conjecture are followed although guidance has come from the Lord, contrasting self-chosen drift with received direction.

luna: The verse promises believers a light “تَمْشُونَ بِهِ” (by which you walk). This image of walking by granted light parallels the section’s route and its landmarks, while making the aid visible along the journey. | terra: Believers are given a light `تَمْشُونَ بِهِ`; the image supplies illumination for walking, akin to the landmarks by which the traveller proceeds.
terra: The earth is made `ذَلُولًا` and people are told to walk its tracts; its subdued walking-ground vividly answers the commentary's softened, traversable path.

luna: The verse asks who is better guided: one who walks “مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ” or one who walks upright “سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ.” Its bodily contrast makes the section’s straight, walkable route perceptible as a way of moving, not only a correctness claim. | terra: The contrast is between one walking fallen on his face and one walking upright on a straight road, a bodily image of walking and orientation on `صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ`.
terra: God makes the earth a spread-out ground, furnishing the surface on which the following ayah's broad roads can be travelled.
terra: `لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا` makes human walking on broad roads the purpose of the spread earth in the preceding ayah.
terra: The jinn hear a Quran that guides `إِلَى الرُّشْدِ`; the response is belief, making the Book a guide toward right direction.

luna: The jinn say some among them are righteous and some otherwise, and “كُنَّا طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا.” Their divided ways concretely echo the section’s image of groups going in every direction rather than sharing one trodden route. | terra: The jinn describe themselves as differing `طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا`, a plurality of diverging ways that makes 6:153's one path and many paths audible.
terra: Those who submit have sought right conduct, while the unjust become fuel for Hell; communal direction has divergent ends.
terra: `اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ` makes continuing steadfastly on a way the condition for abundant provision, joining straight continuance with the sustaining ground of the path.
terra: The reminder is followed by the invitation for whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, an explicit route toward God.

luna: The verse says “إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ” and then names gratitude or ingratitude as the response. It parallels the section’s road with a way shown to a traveller whose subsequent direction is not automatic. | terra: God has guided the human being to `السَّبِيلَ`, after which gratitude and ingratitude divide the response to that shown way.
terra: Whoever wills may take a way to his Lord, again making the goal of guidance a destination rather than information alone.
terra: Moses asks Pharaoh whether he should guide him to his Lord so that he may fear, making guidance an address that leads a person toward God.

luna: After describing the Quran as a reminder, the verse asks “فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ.” This direct question about where people are heading makes the section’s route image an urgent question of direction and choice.

luna: The Quran is a reminder “لِمَن شَاءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَسْتَقِيمَ,” followed by the reminder that human willing depends on God’s will. The shared root of “المستقيم” connects straightness to keeping one’s course, while the context preserves God’s authority over that course.

luna: The verse says “وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ,” that God showed the human being two conspicuous ways. It supplies a concrete fork in the route that sharpens the section’s contrast between walking the favored way and losing it. | terra: `وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ` portrays guidance as showing two rising ways, making a route visible as a choice with divergent outcomes.
terra: `إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ` assigns guidance to God, supporting the prayer's direct address for leading.

luna: God says to the Prophet “وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ.” The section’s lost traveller and its contrast between ضلّ and هدى illuminate this statement while leaving its possible senses of searching or being without guidance open. | terra: `وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ` puts being lost and being guided in the same reversal that frames the plea of 1:6 and its ending in `ٱلضَّآلِّينَ`.
terra: They are commanded to worship God with sincere religion, `ذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ`; worship and upright religion recur as the path's inner practice.
